Estee: English, a short form of Esther or Estelle, from Persian 'star'; also a surname-based name.
Baziel: Flemish form of Basil, from Greek basileus 'king'.
Enzio: Italian and German form of Enzo, from Heinz or Lorenzo; also Enzio as medieval Sardinian king.
Marcos: Spanish and Portuguese form of Mark, from Latin Marcus, possibly linked to Mars.
Adrián: Spanish form of Adrian, Latin 'from Hadria', a town in northern Italy.
Arion: Greek, from a mythical immortal horse and a poet-musician. Meaning uncertain.
Hadia: Arabic, 'calm, quiet' or 'guiding'; feminine of Hadi.
Rahela: Slavic and Romanian form of Rachel, Hebrew 'ewe'.
Rama: Sanskrit, 'pleasing, charming'; the hero of the Ramayana. Also Arabic 'aim, goal'.
Yoko: Japanese, with different kanji such as 'positive child' or 'ocean child'.
Dex: Short form of Dexter, Latin dexter 'right-handed, skilful'.
Ebbe: Scandinavian and Frisian, from Germanic eber 'wild boar'. Short form of Eberhard.
Gabriëlla: Italian-style feminine of Gabriel, Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Frans: Dutch and Scandinavian form of Francis, meaning 'Frenchman' or 'free one'.
Nayah: Probably a modern variant of Naya or Nia; possibly Hebrew or Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Beniamin: Polish and Romanian form of Benjamin, Hebrew 'son of the right hand'.
Matheus: Portuguese and Dutch variant of Matthew, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Narin: Turkish and Kurdish, 'delicate, fine'; also Persian-related.
Polina: Russian form of Paulina, from Latin Paulus 'small, humble'.
Siel: Probably a modern Dutch coinage, perhaps from Siel 'soul' in Frisian or a variant of Ciel. Origin uncertain.
Rafaella: Italian feminine of Raphael, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Enoha: Probably a variant of Enoch, Hebrew 'dedicated, trained'. Origin uncertain.
Tassnim: Arabic Tasnim, a spring in Paradise; 'raised high'.
Leonel: Spanish and Portuguese, from Lionel, French diminutive of Léon, 'lion'.
Marcello: Italian, from Latin Marcellus, a diminutive of Marcus.
Ruiz: Spanish surname meaning 'son of Ruy' or Rodrigo; rare as a first name.
Souhayl: Arabic Suhayl, 'smooth, easy'; also the star Canopus.
Natanael: Spanish and Dutch form of Nathanael, Hebrew 'God has given'.
Seyit: Turkish form of Arabic Sayyid, 'master, lord'.
Tore: Scandinavian, from Old Norse Thórir, 'Thor's warrior'.
Junot: French surname, a name of Napoleon's general; probably from Junon or Jean. Origin uncertain.
Mamoudou: West African form of Arabic Mahmud, 'praised'.
Serra: Turkish name, meaning 'greenhouse'; also Italian and Catalan 'saw, mountain range'.
Poppy: English, from the flower name, ultimately Latin papaver.
Otilia: Spanish and Romanian form of Odile, Germanic 'fortune' or 'prosperous heritage'.
Fatimata: West African form of Fatima, Arabic 'one who abstains'.
Alois: German and Czech form of Aloysius, from Latinised Louis, Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Bernardo: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Bernard, Germanic 'brave bear'.
Izzy: English pet form of Isabel, Isaac or Isidore.
Júlia: Portuguese and Catalan form of Julia, from the Roman clan Julius.
Marlou: Dutch compound of Marie and Lou, or short form of Marlène.
Cooper: English occupational surname meaning 'barrel maker', used as a given name.
Khadidja: French spelling of Khadija, Arabic 'premature child'; first wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Suri: Hebrew, Yiddish form of Sarah 'princess'; also Persian 'red rose'.
Armen: Armenian, probably from Armenia or a form of Armenak. Also an Armenian given name.
Aboubakar: West African form of Abu Bakr, 'father of the young camel'; first caliph of Islam.
Nihel: Arabic Nahil or Nihal; probably 'quenched thirst' or 'young plant'. Uncertain.
Tidiane: West African name, probably from Arabic Tijani, a Sufi order. Origin uncertain.
Fineas: Variant of Phineas, from Hebrew 'serpent's mouth' or Egyptian 'dark-skinned'. Origin partly uncertain.
Malky: Yiddish, a pet form of Malka, Hebrew 'queen'.
Maëlio: Modern French coinage, likely from Breton Maël 'prince'. Origin uncertain.
Ofelia: Spanish and Italian form of Ophelia, from Greek 'help, benefit'.
Yiit: Likely a Turkish spelling variant of Yiğit, 'brave, young hero'.
Charli: Variant of Charlie, English pet form of Charles, Germanic 'free man'.
Salome: Hebrew shalom 'peace'; biblical name of Herod's stepdaughter and a follower of Jesus.
Aws: Arabic, 'gift' or 'wolf'; a tribe of Medina.
Jante: Dutch Frisian girl's name, a pet form of Jantine or Johanna, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Noalie: Modern French coinage, blending Noa and Amélie. Origin uncertain.
Rebeka: Slavic and Scandinavian form of Rebecca, Hebrew possibly 'to bind'.
Simão: Portuguese form of Simon, Hebrew 'he has heard'.
Edem: Ghanaian Ewe name or Turkish Edem; meaning varies. In Ewe it relates to 'God is good'. Origin uncertain.
Juune: Probably a variant of June, from the month, Latin Junius.
Emilya: Variant of Emilia, from Latin Aemilia, a Roman clan name.
Ignazio: Italian form of Ignatius, from Latin ignis 'fire', possibly.
Maro: Possibly Armenian 'Maro' (masculine, from Mary), Greek 'bitter', or Latin Maro, Virgil's family name. Origin uncertain.
El: Hebrew and Semitic, 'God'; also a short form of names such as Elias or Elisabeth.
Juwayriya: Arabic, 'little girl'; a wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Tito: Italian and Spanish form of Titus, Latin of uncertain meaning; also Croatian Tito.
Aeden: Variant of Aidan, Irish Aodhán, from aodh 'fire'.
Jamie-Lee: English compound of Jamie (from James) and Lee, 'meadow'.
Mïa: Variant of Mia, Scandinavian pet form of Maria, or Italian 'mine'.
Arden: English place name meaning 'high valley'; also Latin 'burn, glow'.
Mouhamad: French West African spelling of Muhammad, 'praised'.
Myléna: Probably a variant of Milena or Mylène, from Slavic 'dear' or Greek-related. Origin uncertain.
Anisia: Latinate feminine of Anisius or Greek Anysia, from Greek anysios 'complete'.
Lélio: Portuguese and Italian, from Latin Laelius, a Roman clan name.
Maida: English, probably from the Maida Vale district or Old English 'maiden'. Also Arabic 'table'.
Otta: Probably a pet form of Otto or Ottilie, Germanic 'wealth, fortune'.
Loucia: French variant of Lucia, from Latin lux 'light'.
Marya: Slavic and Arabic form of Mary. Arabic Marya can mean 'white'.
Éowyn: Invented by Tolkien in The Lord of the Rings; Old English 'horse joy' roots.
Zane: English form of John, probably Hebrew 'God is gracious'; Zane Grey made it known.
Wilco: Dutch short form of Wilhelm or Wilke, Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'.
Maddie: English pet form of Madeleine or Madison.
Mati: Short form of Matthias, Hebrew 'gift of God'; also Spanish pet form.
Raphaëlla: Feminine of Raphaël, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Nouraya: Arabic, derived from nur 'light'; a variant of Nuraya.
Timao: Probably a modern variant of Timéo or Timothy, Greek 'honouring God'. Origin uncertain.
Ilyanna: Modern blend of Ilya or Eli with Anna, 'God is my Lord' and 'grace'.
Livie: English pet form of Olivia or Livia.
Alva: Swedish, probably from Old Norse alfr 'elf'; also Spanish/Hebrew-related uses.
Rafi: Arabic Rafi, 'exalted'; also Hebrew short form of Raphael.
Alyx: Modern variant of Alex or Alix; Greek 'defender'.
Hadriel: Probably a modern blend of Hadrian and El, Hebrew 'God'. Origin uncertain.
Alessyo: Variant of Alessio, Italian form of Alexis, Greek 'defender'.
Julieta: Spanish form of Juliet, from Latin Julius.
Abigaelle: French form of Abigail, Hebrew 'my father is joy'.
Louqman: Arabic Luqman, a wise figure in the Quran; meaning uncertain, possibly 'to feed'.
Nalia: Probably a modern coinage or variant of Nahlia or Natalia. Origin uncertain.
Sohann: Probably a variant of Sohan or Johann, or Hindi 'beautiful'. Origin uncertain.
Arsema: Ethiopian (Amharic), possibly 'Arsema', used in Ethiopia and Eritrea. Origin uncertain.
Barlas: Turkic, from the Barlas tribe of Central Asia (Timur's clan).
Billie-Lou: English compound of Billie (from William) and Lou (from Louise).
Jouri: Arabic Jury, a Damask rose; also a Russian short form of Yuri.
Seyana: Probably modern; possibly from Seiana or Cheyenne. Origin uncertain.
Rion: Probably a variant of Ryan or Rio, Spanish 'river'; also Japanese. Origin uncertain.
Avélie: Probably a modern blend of Ava and Amélie or Avelina. Origin uncertain.
Lylio: Probably a modern coinage from Lily or Lyli. Origin uncertain.
Isaïa: French form of Isaiah, Hebrew 'God is salvation'.
Kael: Probably Gaelic Caoil 'slender' or a modern variant of Kyle. Origin uncertain.
Dumitru: Romanian form of Demetrius, Greek 'follower of Demeter'.
Zaira: Spanish and Italian, possibly Arabic zahra 'flower' or Moorish. Origin uncertain.
Alora: Probably a modern coinage, or from Alora, a Spanish town. Origin uncertain.
Willie: English pet form of William, Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'.
Diyan: Possibly Bulgarian or Arabic; in Bulgarian a pet form of Dian. Origin uncertain.
Koa: Hawaiian, 'brave, warrior'; also a native tree.
Nooh: Arabic and Persian spelling of Noah, 'rest, comfort'.
Scottie: English pet form of Scott, 'man from Scotland'.
Émilia: French and Latin form of Aemilia, from the Roman clan Aemilius.
Balqis: Arabic name of the Queen of Sheba, of uncertain meaning.
Loëlya: Modern French coinage, probably blending Lou with Lia or Elya. Origin uncertain.
Tiya: Sanskrit and Hindi, 'bird' or 'sweet'; also an Egyptian queen name Tiye.
Louëlle: Modern French feminine blend of Lou and Elle. Origin uncertain.
Énola: Probably a modern coinage; best known as Enola Gay, or backwards 'alone'. Origin uncertain.
Noée: French feminine form of Noé, from Hebrew Noah 'rest'.
Ézékiel: French form of Ezekiel, Hebrew 'God strengthens'.
Oli: Short form of Oliver, Old French olivier 'olive tree'; or of Olivia.
Yüna: Variant of Yuna, Japanese 'gentle' or Korean 'grace'; origin varies.
Naëlyo: Modern French coinage, from Naël or Noël. Origin uncertain.
Solea: Probably from Latin sol 'sun' or Spanish soledad 'solitude'. Origin uncertain.
Ellie-Mae: English compound of Ellie (from Eleanor) and Mae (from May or Mary).
Ézio: Italian, from Latin Aetius, perhaps 'eagle'; known through the Assassin's Creed series.
Luèn: Probably a variant of Luan or Luen; possibly Breton or Welsh-related. Origin uncertain.
Lyzia: Probably a variant of Lisa or Lydia, or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Tahyssia: Probably a modern variant of Thaïs or Tahisia. Origin uncertain.
Khalys: Probably a variant of Arabic Khalis, 'pure', or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Mykhailo: Ukrainian form of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Parla: Possibly Turkish parla 'shine', or Italian-related. Origin uncertain.
Maiza: Arabic Mayza, 'discerning'; also variant of Maisa.
Soleya: Probably a modern variant of Soleil, French 'sun', or Spanish Soleá. Origin uncertain.
Louaz: Arabic, possibly from Lu'ay or Louay, 'bull' or 'shield'. Origin uncertain.
Jens: Danish and German form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Jelle: Dutch and Frisian, from Germanic gelt 'payment, atonement'.
Brandon: English surname from place names meaning 'broom hill'.
Ine: Dutch and Flemish short form of Catharina or Josephina; also Old English king Ine.
Steven: English and Dutch form of Stephen, Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Sven: Scandinavian, from Old Norse sveinn 'boy, servant'.
Joran: Dutch form of Jorin, a variant of George or Jurre, Greek 'farmer'.
Tiffany: English, from Theophania, Greek 'manifestation of God'.
Killian: Irish Cillian, probably from ceallach 'bright-headed' or 'strife'.
Hannes: German, Dutch and Scandinavian short form of Johannes, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Donovan: Irish surname from Ó Donnabháin, 'descendant of dark one'.
Shania: Ojibwe-claimed 'I'm on my way' (made famous by Shania Twain); origin uncertain.
Bente: Danish and Dutch form of Benedicta, Latin 'blessed'.
Kenji: Japanese, with kanji meaning 'strong second son' or 'wise ruler'.
Melvin: English and Irish, perhaps from Mel plus -vin or Old French 'Malvin'; meaning uncertain.
Renske: Dutch Frisian, pet form of Renata or Reinier, Latin 'reborn'.
Sanae: Japanese, possibly 'sprout' or 'clear' depending on kanji; Arabic Sana'a 'brilliance'.
Jolan: Hungarian, from Yolanda, possibly Greek 'violet flower'; also Dutch variant of Jolien.
Ornella: Italian, coined by D'Annunzio from Latin ornus 'flowering ash'.
Yari: Spanish pet form of Yarely or Yaritza; also Japanese. Origin varies.
Brieuc: Breton, from Welsh Briog, from Welsh 'respected'. Saint Brieuc.
Furkan: Turkish, from Arabic Furqan, 'criterion, discernment'; a name for the Quran.
Stacy: English pet form of Anastasia or Eustace, Greek 'resurrection'.
Jessy: English variant of Jesse or Jessie, Hebrew 'gift' or 'God exists'.
